assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a clear, general principle (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination) that gave a new capability: forming aryl C-N bonds under mild conditions. Its use in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and materials is enormous and easy to explain to a broad audience.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, broadly applicable amination methods and ligand design; Kosugi's earlier stoichiometric tin-amide coupling is a precursor rather than the decisive general method. Two laureates is a clean configuration, though the precursor credit can be argued.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent confirmation and industrial adoption; the interpretation is stable. Timing is mature, arguably late, and the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize adds a mild overlap concern.
uncertainties: Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize makes a C-N-specific citation seem derivative.
Fair weight for Kosugi, Migita and the precursor literature; my recollection of the exact chronology is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA/RNA molecules electrically through a nanopore rests on a physical principle (ionic current blockade by a translocating polymer), and its realization needed nanoscale engineering of pores and motor-controlled translocation. It opened a new measurement capability: long reads, direct RNA and base-modification detection, portable sequencers.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer demonstrated polynucleotide translocation; Bayley engineered protein pores; Akeson and others solved enzymatic ratcheting and base resolution. Credit is spread and contested, and some key figures may be deceased or are only partly in the credited set, so a three-person selection is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Commercially mature and widely validated in genomics; accuracy has improved steadily and independent groups confirm it. Recognition is timely, though a chemistry citation needs a clear molecular-level framing.
uncertainties: Which of Branton, Deamer, Bayley, Kasianowicz and Akeson are eligible and should be named is uncertain.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as physics/biotechnology.
I cannot verify current status of individual nominees.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system, via bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, converts a binder into a degrader and makes previously undruggable targets accessible. This is a new capability with large generative potential, and a unifying mechanistic principle.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept; Handa and colleagues identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, explaining molecular glue mechanism. Ciulli, Gray and others made important later advances. The compound discovery splits into PROTACs and glue mechanism, and assignment of decisive credit is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in trials but approvals are still limited, so the practical impact is partly prospective; mechanistic confirmation is strong. Slightly early relative to peers.
uncertainties: Whether clinical evidence is yet sufficient.
How to split recognition between PROTAC invention and the cereblon/glue mechanism.
Role of Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto in the decisive step.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing chemically converts one base to another in genomic DNA without double-strand breaks, by engineering deaminase-Cas fusions. It is a clean, original molecular design with large therapeutic potential and a clear story for the public.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu's group led the invention and its extension to A-to-G editing, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainees; Nishida and Kondo reported a related cytidine deaminase approach. A single-laureate award for Liu is defensible but the parallel work is a caveat.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly validated across many labs and now in clinical use, though the field is young and prime editing/other advances may reshape the framing. Slightly early.
uncertainties: CRISPR was recognized in 2020, so overlap and framing as chemistry are uncertain.
Credit for parallel Nishida/Kondo work.
Long-term clinical track record is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle for cells brings thermodynamics of condensates into biology, a physicist's concept with broad explanatory power for membraneless organelles. It changed how cell organization is studied and has prompted new drug-discovery ideas.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P-granule liquid behaviour; Rosen provided the reconstituted multivalent-interaction framework; Pappu and Mittag contributed physical-chemical theory. Decisive credit is plausible for three but contested.
assessment.maturity: Highly influential, but debate persists about in vivo physiological relevance, artifacts of overexpression and how general the principle is. Interpretation is still evolving, so possibly premature.
uncertainties: In vivo relevance and specificity of condensate function.
Whether this is chemistry or cell biology.
Attribution between experimental and theory contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites as solar absorbers show remarkable efficiency growth from a simple solution-processable material, with unusual defect tolerance and long carrier lifetimes that raise interesting physics questions. Impact on photovoltaics research is large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first reported perovskite-sensitized cells; Park, Grätzel and Snaith made decisive efficiency and architecture advances; Kanatzidis and Seok also contributed. The three-person choice excludes strong contributors, so attribution is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation of efficiency is solid, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial deployment remain unresolved. Recognition would be early.
uncertainties: Stability and commercialization.
Complex credit among six names.
Mechanistic understanding of defect tolerance remains partial.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy-landscape and funnel theory gave protein folding a quantitative physical framework, resolving the Levinthal paradox and linking statistical mechanics to biochemistry. It connects well with my own view of non-equilibrium and thermodynamic principles and had broad conceptual influence.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson built the funnel/landscape theory; Dill advanced hydrophobic-collapse models; Fersht provided experimental mapping. Allocating theory versus experiment is delicate.
assessment.maturity: The framework is decades old and well established, and its practical power was partly demonstrated by predictive tools, though 2024's prize already recognized structure prediction.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 protein-structure prize.
Distinguishing the theory from later refinements.
Fersht's experimental role would be omitted in my selection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: CO-tip non-contact AFM resolves the bond structure of individual molecules, a vivid, quantitative demonstration that directly images chemical bonds and on-surface reactions. As a physicist I value the clarity and the new capability, although the scope is mainly surface science.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl developed qPlus sensor technology; Gross, Meyer and colleagues demonstrated bond-resolved imaging with CO-functionalized tips. Eigler and Ho belong to an adjacent STM lineage. A three-person selection is plausible but arbitrary at the margin.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, and used to identify unknown structures and track reactions; yet its general use in chemistry is still limited by sample and substrate constraints.
uncertainties: Breadth of impact beyond specialist surface-science settings.
Whether the committee views it as chemistry or physics.
Inclusion of Eigler or Ho.
